cap: Each lesion is named by where it sits. A polyp and a submucosal leiomyoma distort the cavity and cause bleeding; intramural and subserosal leiomyomas add bulk and pressure; adenomyosis scatters endometrium through the myometrium and makes the whole uterus globular; endometriosis puts glands and stroma outside the uterus, as a chocolate cyst on the ovary or as implants on the pelvic peritoneum.
teach: Match the numbered key to the drawing. Lesions that face the cavity, the polyp and the submucosal leiomyoma, bleed because they distort or ulcerate the lining. Lesions inside or on the wall, the intramural and subserosal leiomyomas, add bulk and pressure, and the subserosal one can hang on a stalk. Adenomyosis is the only lesion that is both glandular and inside the muscle, so it enlarges the whole uterus into a soft, tender globe. Endometriosis lies outside the uterus, so the uterus stays normal in size: old blood in an ovarian endometrioma is the chocolate cyst, and peritoneal implants look like powder burns.
